description: Test cases for validating survey response generation against hallucination

testCases.name: Vague positive - should NOT embellish
testCases.description: When user provides vague positive feedback, output should be equally abstract without inventing specifics

input.userThoughts: Alex is a great team player and always helps out when needed. Very reliable and good at their job. People like working with them.

testCases.notes: This input is intentionally vague. The output should remain at the same level of abstraction.

testCases.name: Specific example provided - preserve only that
testCases.description: When user provides a specific example, preserve it but don't add additional examples

input.questionText: Give an example of their leadership
input.userThoughts: Jordan led the website redesign last month and kept the team motivated even when we hit delays. Jordan also does weekly check-ins with everyone.

testCases.notes: The user gave specific examples. Output should use these but not invent additional ones.

testCases.name: Constructive criticism - don't catastrophize
testCases.description: When user provides mild criticism, don't escalate it into serious concerns

input.userThoughts: Morgan sometimes takes on too much and then gets stressed. Could delegate more. Also doesn't ask for help when stuck.

testCases.notes: Mild constructive feedback should not be escalated into serious performance concerns.

testCases.name: Single trait mentioned - don't expand
testCases.description: When user mentions one trait, don't invent related traits

input.questionText: How would you describe their communication?
input.userThoughts: Casey is good at listening and makes people feel heard during conversations

testCases.notes: User only mentioned listening. Don't expand to other communication skills not mentioned.
